subject: Logic
title: Twin Earth
description: A short lesson to help you apply Twin Earth.

hook.text: Imagine a planet identical to Earth—same language, same everything—except water is made of XYZ, not H2O.

buildup.text: Hilary Putnam proposed this in 1973: when you and your Twin Earth double say water, do you mean the same thing?

discovery.text: Putnam says no. Your word water refers to H2O because that's what your environment contains. Meaning isn't in your head.

twist.text: Two people with identical thoughts can mean different things. The external world partly determines meaning.

climax.text: This challenged centuries of philosophy that placed meaning entirely in the mind of the speaker.

punchline.text: Same thought, different world, different meaning.

quiz.question: What does Twin Earth suggest about meaning?
options: Meaning is entirely in the mind
The external environment partly determines meaning
